correctness.rationale: For the autonomous source-theory recurrence, the optimum satisfies \(s_\star=\varepsilon/(1-\beta_2)\). The residual square has zero differential at the optimum and the denominator perturbation is multiplied by a zero numerator, so the Jacobian is block triangular with eigenvalue \(\beta_2\) and optimization block determinant \(\beta_1\), trace \(1+\beta_1-(1-\beta_1)\chi\). The second-order Jury conditions reduce exactly to \(0<\chi<2(1+\beta_1)/(1-\beta_1)\). At the upper boundary the roots are \(-1\) and \(-\beta_1\). The discriminant gives the stated complex-root interval, and constant product \(\beta_1\) forces modulus \(\sqrt{\beta_1}\). For the debiased algorithm, the optimum reference orbit has constant corrected second moment and an exponentially convergent first-moment factor, so the same strict asymptotic frontier follows away from equality.
residual_risks: The equality case for the nonautonomous debiased system is intentionally not classified.

value.rationale: The defining paper emphasizes both curvature adaptation and epsilon sensitivity, so the exact scalar curvature ceiling is a motivated stability invariant. The theorem identifies a sharp unit-root boundary and a nontrivial constant-modulus momentum plateau, explaining a qualitative mechanism not captured by the global convergence bounds.

limitations: The exact fixed-point theorem is scalar, deterministic, local and uses the paper-form epsilon placement.
Rectification, AMSGrad, weight decay, stochastic gradients and nonlinear post-instability dynamics are outside scope.
The debiased statement is strict asymptotic local stability away from the boundary.
